sections.h2: How is property tax handled in Metcalfe County?
sections.html:
Metcalfe County runs property tax through offices in Edmonton: the PVA (Property Valuation Administrator) assesses, the sheriff bills and collects, and the county clerk takes over delinquent bills in the spring. The county's own PVA site, hosted on qpublic.net, publishes the roll and a tax calendar.

Edmonton is both the county seat and the only incorporated city in the county.

sections.h2: Where is Metcalfe County and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Metcalfe County is a south central Kentucky county of about 290 square miles, set off in May 1860 and named for Thomas Metcalfe, the state's governor from 1828 to 1832. The county site calls it the 106th county created in Kentucky. It belongs to the Glasgow micropolitan area, part of the Bowling Green and Glasgow combined statistical area. Summer Shade is a census designated place, and Alone is listed as a ghost town.

Edmonton sits on the Louis B. Nunn Cumberland Parkway. The county site puts Interstate 65 about 29 miles away by that road, Glasgow 16 miles west, Louisville 113 miles away, Lexington 124, and Nashville 112. U.S. 68 and Kentucky routes 80 and 163 also serve the town. CSX rail service is near Glasgow, and Moore Field there has a 4,586 foot paved runway.

Neighboring counties are Hart, Green, Adair, Cumberland, Monroe and Barren. A seller should expect buyers who commute toward Glasgow or Bowling Green, and should price against homes in that wider area.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about the Metcalfe County housing market?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census found 10,286 residents, up slightly from 10,099 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 10,583. The 2020 count also listed 4,691 housing units, of which 11.6 percent were vacant, and all of the population was rural.

From the 2020 to 2024 survey:

  • Owners occupy 77.7 percent of homes, the highest rate among these four counties.
  • Owners with a mortgage report $1,066 a month in costs, and owners without one report $368.
  • Total employment in 2023 was 1,234, a drop of 7.5 percent from 2022.
  • Mean time to work is 25.9 minutes, the shortest of the four.

sections.h2: Which Metcalfe County offices handle tax questions?
sections.html:
The county's elected officials page lists these contacts.

  • Sheriff: bills and collections. P.O. Box 371, Edmonton, KY 42129, phone (270) 432-3041.
  • PVA: values, exemption forms, mailing address changes. P.O. Box 939, phone (270) 432-3162, and the site is www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.
  • Fiscal Court: county government at 201 North Main Street, P.O. Box 149, phone (270) 432-3181.
  • County Attorney: P.O. Box 999, phone (270) 432-0777.

Ask the county clerk's office for lien and delinquent bill information. The PVA site adds that a new owner who gets no bill should contact the sheriff.

sections.h2: Why do the Metcalfe County payment dates look different from the state's?
sections.html:
The state statute, KRS 134.015, sets November 1 as the end of the 2 percent discount. The Metcalfe County PVA's calendar page instead lists November 30 for the discount, December 1 to 31 at face value, and delinquency on January 1. Check the dates printed on your own bill and confirm with the sheriff before you rely on the later date.

The PVA calendar also lists these steps:

  • Bills reach the sheriff by September 15.
  • A 5 percent penalty applies from January 1 to 31.
  • After January 31, a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent sheriff add-on fee apply.
  • Unpaid bills move to the county clerk after the sheriff closes on April 15.
  • The clerk's sale of delinquent certificates falls between July 14 and August 28, and the sheriff's settlement is due by September 1.

sections.h2: How can you appeal a Metcalfe County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet the PVA first, during the public inspection of the roll that opens on the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days, six days a week including Saturday. After a conference that fails, you file with the county clerk no later than the next workday after the window closes.

Three local residents sit on the board of assessment appeals, and the mayor of the largest city in the county, the fiscal court and the judge executive appoint them. Because Edmonton is the only city, its mayor makes one of the picks. The board must explain in writing any change it makes, and taxpayers may record the hearing.

  • Bring the sale price and date of any similar home near yours.
  • Include a contractor quote for repairs the PVA record does not show.
  • State the dollar value you claim on the form.

If you file and then skip the hearing, you cannot take the appeal further.

sections.h2: How is rural land valued in Metcalfe County?
sections.html:
Kentucky PVAs must see every parcel at least once every four years and add new buildings to the roll each year. Farm land may be assessed at its agricultural value rather than its fair cash value, according to the Department of Revenue.

With nearly 290 square miles and a population of about 10,500, many Metcalfe County sales include acreage. If part of a parcel is farmed, ask the PVA how it is classified before you list.

sections.h2: Who can claim the homestead exemption in Metcalfe County?
sections.html:
A Metcalfe County resident who turns 65 during the year, or who is classified as totally disabled on January 1, can apply at the PVA for the home they own and live in. KRS 132.810 limits it to one exemption per residential unit, and it covers mobile homes and manufactured houses.

A disabled owner under 65 must reapply every year unless the person is a service connected totally disabled veteran or has a permanent disability finding. The tax savings are credited if you apply before paying, and refunded if you apply afterward.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Metcalfe County taxes?
sections.html:
On April 15 the unpaid bills become certificates of delinquency at the clerk's office, each with a recorded lien. The state adds 1 percent interest monthly, a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee. The clerk must advertise the list at least 30 days before the sale.

Under KRS 134.015 the tax is a personal debt of whoever owned on January 1, and the lien can follow the property for 11 years. If a private buyer gets the certificate, the owner then pays that buyer and may face further fees.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Metcalfe County house with back taxes?
sections.html:
You can. The payoff comes from the sheriff before April 15 and the clerk afterward, and it grows each month once the clerk holds it. Ask for a written figure dated close to your closing.

Tax ownership is set on January 1, so a house sold later in the year is billed to the former owner until the next year. Many Metcalfe County sellers hold older houses with deferred repairs. Compare a cash offer and a listing by working out the net after repairs, tax and months of carrying cost.

faqs.q: Who collects Metcalfe County property tax?
faqs.a: The Metcalfe County Sheriff collects it. The office is at P.O. Box 371 in Edmonton, and the phone is (270) 432-3041.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in Edmonton?
faqs.a: Edmonton is the county's only incorporated city. Ask the Fiscal Court at (270) 432-3181 whether a city bill applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the Metcalfe County PVA phone number?
faqs.a: The PVA's number is (270) 432-3162, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 939, Edmonton, KY 42129.

faqs.q: When does the assessment appeal window open in Metcalfe County?
faqs.a: It opens on the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days. You must meet with the PVA before you can file an appeal.

faqs.q: How long can a tax lien stay on a Metcalfe County house?
faqs.a: Up to 11 years under KRS 134.015, no matter who owns the house in the meantime.
